new_scholarship.description: The University of Brescia awards two four-year STAR 'Students at Risk' scholarships covering a one-year Foundation Year in A.Y. 2026/27 followed by an Italian-taught bachelor's degree from A.Y. 2027/28. Each scholarship is worth EUR 6,132.10 and additionally waives Foundation Year and, if renewed, undergraduate tuition, provides free shared accommodation in university residences, a subsidised canteen place, a discounted public transport pass and EUR 500 towards National Health Service enrolment or private health insurance. Candidates must hold nationality and residence in a developing country under Italian Ministerial Decree no. 166/2025 or in Cuba, Egypt, El Salvador, Jordan, Iraq, Kenya, Lebanon, Tunisia or the Palestinian Territories; one scholarship is reserved for African candidates.

One of the two scholarships is reserved for candidates from African countries whose secondary-school diploma was also obtained in an African country.

new_scholarship.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of China (Taiwan) grants the Taiwan Scholarship to encourage outstanding international students to study in Taiwan and to promote bilateral exchanges with Taiwan's diplomatic allies. Degree-programme recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 (NT$28,000 for the one-year pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program) plus one-way economy-class airfare, while remaining responsible for all expenses during their stay. The scholarship is, in principle, granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, is not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, and is applied for through the local ROC overseas representative office between 1 February and 31 March each year.

The scholarship is in principle for students from countries with diplomatic relations with Taiwan, though special consideration may be given to others.

new_scholarship.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship in 2005 to encourage international students and individuals to undertake Mandarin Chinese language study in Taiwan at a university- or college-affiliated Mandarin training centre. The scholarship provides a fixed monthly stipend of NT$28,000 with no other subsidy, and may be used for a two-month summer course or for three, six, nine or twelve months of study. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over and must apply through the authorised ROC overseas office in their country of nationality; the exact deadline is set by that office.

new_scholarship.description: The Taiwan Ministry of Education created the Elite Scholarship Program to encourage lecturers from countries in South and Southeast Asia, as well as Africa, to pursue a graduate degree in Taiwan. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$25,000, amounting to NT$300,000 (approximately USD 10,000) per year, which the Ministry issues as funding for tuition and credit fees with the remainder used as a monthly stipend. The award runs for three years in PhD programmes and two years in master's programmes, reviewed annually, and is awarded on the basis of a college recommendation and scholarship committee review rather than a direct student application. For the 2026/27 academic year NCKU required a lecturer certificate and application by 23 September 2026.

A separate track covers applicants from all African countries who are lecturers or professors, with an employment certificate and research publications required. MOE states the award is based on a college recommendation and scholarship committee review, not a direct student application.
